story.title: The Empty Chair — dialogue cut
story.logline: A reserved café regular makes room for a stranger, begins saving his seat, and discovers their brief connection mattered to him too.
story.character_notes: The protagonist has a shaded white round head, white torso and navy limbs. The visitor wears a muted teal scarf. Keep the rust-orange bag, sage cups, round wooden table, left window and rear-right green door consistent.

scenes.narration: Every morning, she drew at the same café. And every morning, her bag took the other chair.
scenes.visual: Morning café. She draws alone on the left, with her orange bag occupying the right chair.

scenes.narration: Until someone asked, “Mind if I sit?”
scenes.visual: The teal-scarf visitor stands beside the chair and gestures toward it. She looks up tentatively.
She leans across and lifts the orange bag off the right chair, making room for him.

scenes.narration: He noticed her sketchbook. “Wait... you drew this?” They talked until their coffee went cold.
scenes.visual: Both seated, she shows him her detailed café sketch. He gestures appreciatively; she smiles.

scenes.narration: The next morning, she saved his seat. Then the next.
scenes.visual: The right chair is empty. She pauses drawing and looks hopefully toward the empty entrance.

scenes.narration: By the fourth morning, the bag was back.
scenes.visual: Bag on the right chair again. Her shoulders slump and her expression is disappointed.

scenes.narration: That's when she heard, “I tried drawing our table.” He held up a sketchbook. Crooked legs. Cups like potatoes.
scenes.visual: He returns holding his clumsy drawing. Her face lights up and she reaches toward his chair.

scenes.narration: She laughed, moved her bag... and pulled out his chair.
scenes.visual: Closing overhead shot of two sketchbooks, her accomplished drawing beside his wobbly attempt. Two cups and two hands share the table.
